headline: A rough month for swing trades, but it's too early to judge, and options had a good day.

points.label: Swing
points.text: In a trend system the closed trades are mostly the stopped-out losers, because the winners are still running, so read this next to the open book. Most of this month's closed trades were stopped out, which is a small sample (15 trades) and not yet a verdict. Losses are running bigger than wins, and the usual win rate for this strategy is low anyway, so the real test is whether the occasional big winner shows up. The market is in a healthy uptrend, which makes a losing month worth watching rather than excusing. It's too early to say you're getting better, as there's almost nothing earlier to compare with. Today brought 5 entry signals and 2 exit signals, and the 7 trades closed today lost a little (Rs896). The open book is still comfortably more winners than losers.

points.label: Options
points.text: Two option contracts closed today and both made money, Rs5,600 together (HCLTECH and BSE). Both were bought back at the profit target, which is how the plan is meant to work, and the 3x stop did not fire. Two trades prove nothing yet. Judge the strategy after about 30 closed trades, by what the winners make against what the occasional loser costs. Your trend exit comes first and the 3x stop is only the backstop for a gap, so what matters is how rarely that stop fires. Volatility is on the high side (India VIX about 17.7), so premiums are fatter than usual, which helps sellers. The one thing out of line is the BSE short call sitting against a green trend, which is the real drag. No stock has earned the label 'favourite' yet.

points.label: Events
points.text: Nothing is due in the next three weeks for the stocks you trade options on, and none of your open option positions runs through a results or dividend date. The next busy stretch is January and February, when the quarterly results come out. Start planning now: any short option that expires after a results date should be closed or rolled before that date. For swing stocks outside your option list I have no results dates, so check them yourself before adding to a position.

points.label: Risk management
points.text: You passed 5 of 6 discipline checks today. The one miss is the BSE short call that goes against the green trend, so close it at tomorrow's open. Ten of your swing positions are down more than 6%. From 30 November you will not average these: they ride to their Supertrend exit or get stopped out. If everything hit its exit line today, the book would lose Rs19,249 in total, which is small. On options, a 5% market fall would cost under 1% of capital even if none of your exits acted, so the book is comfortable. The one position that could really hurt is BSE if it jumps sharply, and that is exactly the short call to close.

action: Close the BSE 4200CE in the Dhan app at tomorrow's open, and keep logging trades: it takes about 30 closed trades before any rule change is justified.
